findings.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 uses invalid Ruby syntax `<%- end if %>`, causing existing-topic embed rendering to fail with a template error; use `<%- end %>`.
app/models/post.rb:133 returns unsanitized imported feed HTML through `raw`, allowing scripts and event-handler attributes to cause stored XSS because TopicEmbed.import only rewrites URLs.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34 calls `i.content.scrub` without handling missing content, causing the entire poll to abort for RSS items with only description or Atom entries with only summary; support fallback fields and absent bodies.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 incorrectly rewrites protocol-relative URLs against the article host, breaking imported links and images; resolve references against the article URL using URI resolution.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 returns unsanitized imported feed HTML through `raw`, allowing scripts and event-handler attributes to cause stored XSS because TopicEmbed.import only rewrites URLs.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook() method in post.rb returns `raw` directly without any sanitization. In TopicEmbed.import(), content is passed through absolutize_urls() which only modifies href/src attributes but does NOT sanitize HTML. The content comes from RSS feeds (poll_feed.rb uses CGI.unescapeHTML on content) or from ruby-readability (import_remote). While ruby-readability has a tags whitelist, the RSS feed path in poll_feed.rb passes content directly. The imported content with cook_method[:raw_html] bypasses the normal post cooking/sanitization pipeline. This means malicious HTML from RSS feeds (script tags, event handlers) could be stored and rendered, creating a stored XSS vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 incorrectly rewrites protocol-relative URLs against the article host, breaking imported links and images; resolve references against the article URL using URI resolution.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 53-72, the absolutize_urls method checks if href/src start_with?('/') before prepending the prefix. Protocol-relative URLs (starting with '//') would match this condition since they start with '/'. The code would then incorrectly transform '//example.com/image.jpg' into 'http://eviltrout.com//example.com/image.jpg' (after the sub removes leading slashes, it becomes 'http://eviltrout.com/example.com/image.jpg'). This is a real bug - protocol-relative URLs should be handled differently than root-relative URLs.
